subject: Braeburn: Stability readout & remediation sprint coordination
messages:
From: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@braeburn.ai>
To: tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com
Cc: ops@braeburn.ai
Date: 2027-01-09T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Production latency & 5xx spike right now

Hi Tessa —

We started seeing a latency increase across multiple endpoints around 08:45 PT today and an uptick in 5xx responses from the /generate route. Traffic is normal but tail latency is up and our customers are seeing failed requests. Can you confirm whether there is an ongoing issue on your side?

We captured a short window of metrics and a few sample traces (attached). This is affecting checkout flows for a small subset of users. We need a triage call if you can join within the hour.

Thanks,
Sarah
Senior SRE, Braeburn Retail
[Attachment: braeburn_daily-metrics.csv]
[Attachment: braeburn_latency_logs-jan09.zip]

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@braeburn.ai>, ops@braeburn.ai
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-01-09T09:28:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Production latency & 5xx spike right now

Sarah —

Thanks for the alert and the attachments. We're pulling traces now and standing up an incident bridge. Jonas and Ben are joining the bridge for routing and model-level checks. Can you confirm whether the failed requests are coming from the same model variant (model-id in the csv)? If you can paste a sample request id we can pull the kv-cache and model logs quickly.

I will update in the bridge; aiming for first readout within 30 minutes.

- Tessa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: joining-bridge.txt]

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-01-09T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: INTERNAL: initial triage notes (Braeburn spike)

Team —

Quick notes from the bridge:
- Scope: ~2.8k requests/min for Braeburn tenant between 08:45–09:05 PT; 95th latency jumped from 220ms -> 1.2s. 5xx rate peaked at 0.9%.
- Immediate hypothesis: degraded KV-cache locality after an autoscaler event; a small percentage of requests hit a cold path causing heavy kernel fallbacks.
- Evidence: machine-level logs show a scale event in the pool at 08:42; model runtime logs show extra re-compilation warnings on 7% of sessions.

Action items we kicked off (owner):
1) Force-warm the KV caches for the Braeburn pool (Ben).
2) Pin their traffic to a stable node group to avoid further scale churn (Kimberly).
3) Collect full model runtime traces and share a readout deck for leadership (Tessa).

I captured a dump of the runtime trace window and uploaded it to the Braeburn folder.

Jonas
Head of Reliability
[Attachment: runtime-traces-window.log]

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@braeburn.ai>
Date: 2027-01-11T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Stability readout: findings and proposed sprint (draft deck attached)

Marissa / Jonas —

Per Sarah's request and the exec ask from Braeburn, I'm sending a concise readout and a proposed 5-day remediation sprint to address the latency and error-rate regressions. High level: the issue was triggered by an autoscaler event that increased kernel-selection variance and caused cold-path fallbacks for a subset of sessions. That amplification is what drove the tail latency and a small increase in 5xx.

Attached is the readout deck for leadership. Key pages to review:
- Slide 3: timeline & observed impact (customer-visible metrics)
- Slide 5: root cause summary and evidence links
- Slide 7: sprint scope and success criteria (95th latency < 350ms, error rate < 0.1% stabilization window)
- Slide 9: rollback and fallback playbook if we see recurrence.

Proposed sprint owners:
- Warm/persist KV caches for Braeburn pool (Ben)
- Apply pinning policy to Braeburn traffic (Kimberly)
- Add kernel-selection probe and alert (Jonas)
- Run focused load tests against the pinned pool (Marissa)

Sarah, Alex — can you confirm this approach and whether you want Redwood to run the smoke tests in their staging first or in production with canary traffic?

Attachments: stability-readout-deck-v1.pptx

Thanks,
Tessa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference | 1 Letterman Drive
[Attachment: stability-readout-deck-v1.pptx]

From: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@braeburn.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, Alex Montoya <alex@braeburn.ai>
Date: 2027-01-11T15:20:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Stability readout: findings and proposed sprint (draft deck attached)

Thanks for the speedy analysis and the deck. Braeburn leadership reviewed and wants Redwood to proceed with the remediation sprint beginning Monday (01/11) and to run the verification in their production environment with a 5% canary. We prefer Redwood to execute the warm/pinning and then we'll run our synthetic checks and report back. Please coordinate times for the warm and pin steps so our ops can monitor.

Question: will the pinning change any SLA guarantees or require a config rollback window we should be aware of?

Sarah
Senior SRE, Braeburn Retail

> On Jan 11, 2027, at 11:03 AM, Tessa Morgan wrote:
> > Attachments: stability-readout-deck-v1.pptx

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@braeburn.ai>, Alex Montoya <alex@braeburn.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-01-16T16:45:00-08:00
Subject: Sprint retrospective & next commitments (Braeburn remediation)

Sarah / Alex —

Wrapping up the sprint today. Short summary of results:
- Warm/persist KV cache applied to Braeburn pool on 01/11 at 09:00 PT.
- Pinning policy put in place (traffic affinity to stable node group) on 01/12 at 03:00 PT.
- 5% production canary run between 01/12–01/14; observed 95th latency dropped to 320ms and 5xx rate averaged 0.06% during verification windows.

Outstanding items and owners:
- Instrument kernel-selection probe into the main alerting stack (Jonas) — target completion 01/21.
- Add automated cache-warming after any autoscaler event (Ben) — target completion 01/20.
- Post-change SLA note and runbook update (Marissa) — target completion 01/22.

We uploaded the final readout deck and runtime traces to the shared drive and opened a HubSpot note on DEAL-2026-0387 with the sprint artifacts. If Braeburn is comfortable we can consider this incident closed from a mitigation standpoint; we'll keep the probes on for 14 days of heightened observation.

Thanks for the partnership — reach out if you want a short exec-level 15-minute sync next week.

- Tessa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachments: stability-readout-deck-v1.pptx, braeburn_latency_logs-jan09.zip]
